author: Inside Edition
description: In an image of President Donald Trump and his top advisors, they all wore the same Florsheim shoes, the president's favorite brand. Trumps gives them out as gifts. "All the boys have them," a White House official told The Wall Street Journal. Trump reportedly guesses your shoe size and then sends you the shoes in a signed box. The leather wing-tip dress show is priced at about $145 a pair. The president apparently also gives out shirts.
title: President Trump Reportedly Gifts Advisors The Same Florsheim Shoes

author: Inside Edition
description: One hour before one bride was supposed to walk down the aisle, she fell off a chair. Jordan Downing, 25, looked at her leg and said "a chunk of skin was missing." Friends and family tended to the bride-to-be. Wedding guest Dr. Raj Chowdhury, a plastic surgeon, knew that Downing needed stitches. Chowdhury cleaned and bandaged Downing's thigh so she could make it to her wedding on time. When the wedding was over, Downing went to the hospital where she received 30 stitches.
title: Bride Injured Leg 1 Hour Before Wedding, Gets 30 Stitches After

author: Inside Edition
description: In 1984, 35-year-old Michael Larson became the luckiest man in America as a contestant on the hit CBS game show "Press Your Luck." It turned out that the unemployed ice cream truck driver figured out there was a definite pattern in the game after watching old episodes. Larson ended up winning $110,237 in cash and prizes. The movie "The Luckiest Man In America" is based off Larson's story and is now streaming on Hulu. The movie's director Samie Oliveros spoke with Inside Edition.
title: Movie Based On 'Press Your Luck's' Historic Contestant Now Streaming

author: Inside Edition
description: Heartbreaking footage shows Nancy Guthrie in the bedroom from where she was taken in the early hours of February 1. The live shot from the Tucson bedroom was one of many "Today" show appearances over the years from the missing 84-year-old. One of the show's segments in 2013 was about how to make a bed with "hospital corners" and Nancy Guthrie was called in. As the segment ended, Savannah Guthrie said goodbye to her mother, who got up at 3:00 a.m. to be live on her daughter's show.
title: Resurfaced 'Today' Show Segment From 2013 Shows Nancy Guthrie's Bedroom

author: Inside Edition
description: Two sisters took their very first ride in a driverless Waymo when the car tried to get across a four lane of a highway so it could make a left into another four lanes of traffic. Then, it stopped in the path of oncoming traffic. Waymo tells Inside Edition “while the event does not reflect the vast majority of our services, we take it seriously to learn and improve from it.”
title: Sisters' Waymo Ride Almost Ends In Nightmare #shorts

author: Inside Edition
description: Police in Florida say a traffic stop for speeding turned up a missing child from North Carolina. The Putnam County Sheriff says Joshua Magraff, 37, was pulled over with a female passenger in his car. Deputies say they asked the passenger for identifying information, but they say she gave them false information three times. Investigators say when she finally gave them her real name, she came up as a missing child. Inside Edition Digital’s Mara Montalbano has more.
title: Man Arrested When Found Driving With Missing Child From North Carolina Found
